prompt:
TASK:
            How do you use definite and indefinite forms of nouns in Swedish? Give simple examples.

            PREVIOUS BEST DRAFT (score: 3.2/5.0):
            ---
            Definite form: Man säger att "barnet" är bäst.
Indefinite form: Man säger att "ett barn" är bäst.
            ---

            REVISION INSTRUCTIONS:
            Rewrite the draft above to address the following issues.
            Preserve what was already working well. Do not simply patch — rewrite
            sections where issues are deep.


The following issues MUST be fixed in this revision:
  ✗ [FC-001] Factual Correctness: Inadequate explanation of Swedish definite and indefinite noun forms and their grammatical rules. (flagged 2 times)
  ✗ [CC-001] Clarity & Communication: Lack of context and explanation accompanying examples of definite and indefinite forms. (flagged 2 times)
  ✗ [DC-001] Depth & Completeness: Insufficient depth in explaining the grammatical rules for noun forms in Swedish. (flagged 2 times)

            Produce the improved version now. Output only the revised text, no preamble.
generated_text:
Definite form: Man säger att "barnets" är bäst.
Indefinite form: Man säger att "ett barn" är bäst.

Definite and indefinite forms of nouns in Swedish are used to indicate whether the noun is specific or not. "Barnet" (the child) is definite, while "ett barn" (a child) is indefinite.
